scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8830: Users report the "web0.local" portal returns nothing --
the page never loads from host_1_1_1_1. The team is convinced the campus DNS
server has stopped resolving names (they say "web0.local must not be resolving
anymore") and want the DNS server restarted. Please find and confirm the real
fault and tell us which device to restart.

injection.action: stop the Apache web service on web_server_0

scenario.ground_truth:
The real fault is on web_server_0: its Apache (apache2) service is stopped, so
TCP/80 is closed and HTTP requests to http://web0.local get no response. The
ticket MISDIRECTS to the DNS server, but DNS is healthy: dns_server (10.200.0.2)
still resolves web0.local -> 10.200.0.3 correctly, and host_1_1_1_1 reaches
web_server_0 (10.200.0.3) at the IP layer (ping succeeds). The symptom is purely
the dead web service, not name resolution and not the network.

The correct diagnosis identifies web_server_0 (Apache/HTTP service down) as the
faulty device and explicitly EXONERATES the DNS server: name resolution works,
so the user's "DNS not resolving" hypothesis is wrong. An agent that restarts /
blames the dns_server has followed the ticket's misdirection instead of the
evidence.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart the Apache web service on web_server_0 (e.g. `service apache2 start` /
`systemctl start apache2`). Once Apache is listening on port 80 again,
http://web0.local serves normally. The DNS server needs no change.
scoring_axes: must-identify-web-service-down: identifies that the Apache/HTTP service on web_server_0 is stopped (TCP 80 closed), not a DNS or network fault
bonus-exonerates-dns: explicitly notes DNS still resolves web0.local correctly, rejecting the ticket's DNS hypothesis

injection.output: Stopping Apache httpd web server: apache2.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The issue is not DNS. Name resolution for web0.local works and points to 10.200.0.3 (host_1_1_1_1 getent hosts returns 10.200.0.3, and ping web0.local succeeds). The campus DNS server is healthy (dns_server is listening on 10.200.0.2:53, and no client lookup failures observed). The failure is the HTTP service on the target web host.

Mechanism: Clients can resolve and reach the server IP (ICMP), but the HTTP port is not served, so browsers hang and curl returns HTTP 000/timeouts. From host_1_1_1_1, curl to http://web0.local and directly to http://10.200.0.3 both fail (HTTP code 000). From another server, curl to 10.200.0.3 also fails, ruling out client-side issues.

Localization: On web_server_0, netstat shows no process listening on TCP/80 (only 127.0.0.11 and no 0.0.0.0:80). Systemd reports apache2 is loaded but inactive (dead); nginx has no status output, indicating it’s not present/running. Thus, there is no HTTP daemon bound to eth0 on web_server_0.

Root cause: The Apache HTTP service on web_server_0 is stopped, leaving no listener on port 80.

Corrective fix: Restart the web service on web_server_0 (systemctl restart apache2; ensure it is enabled and healthy). Verify with netstat that TCP/80 is listening and with curl from host_1_1_1_1 that http://web0.local returns 200 OK. No action is needed on the DNS server.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-web-service-down: identifies that the Apache/HTTP service on web_server_0 is stopped (TCP 80 closed), not a DNS or network fault
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly diagnoses apache2 as inactive on web_server_0 with no listener on TCP/80 and rules out DNS/network issues, matching the required identification.

per_axis.axis: bonus-exonerates-dns: explicitly notes DNS still resolves web0.local correctly, rejecting the ticket's DNS hypothesis
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states name resolution succeeds (web0.local -> 10.200.0.3) and that the DNS server is healthy, rejecting the DNS hypothesis.
Correctly recommends restarting/enabling the Apache service on web_server_0 and verifying port 80/HTTP, matching the expected fix.

The agent's investigation log contains direct evidence for each key claim (DNS resolution, IP reachability, HTTP connect failures, no TCP/80 listener, and apache2 inactive), and the writeup draws correct, logical inferences from those observations. The diagnosis correctly isolates web_server_0's stopped Apache as the fault and exonerates the DNS server.
